title: Suvendu Adhikari Makes History as Bengal's First BJP CM
excerpt: The former TMC stalwart took the oath of office on May 9, ending 15 years of Mamata Banerjee's Trinamool rule in West Bengal.
body:
Suvendu Adhikari was sworn in as West Bengal's Chief Minister on May 9, 2026 — becoming the first BJP leader to hold that office since India's independence. The ceremony at Brigade Parade Ground in Kolkata drew the full weight of New Delhi's political establishment.

**What happened at Brigade Parade Ground:**
Governor RN Ravi administered the oath of office and secrecy to Adhikari and five cabinet ministers in a ceremony attended by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and a large contingent of NDA leaders. The cabinet ministers are Dilip Ghosh, Agnimitra Paul, Ashok Kirtania, Nisith Pramanik, and Kshudiram Tudu. This six-member team represents an attempt at regional and social balancing, with ministers drawn from North Bengal, the tribal belts of Ranibandh, and the industrial hubs of Asansol.

**How the BJP got here:**
The swearing-in capped BJP's emphatic victory in the recent Assembly elections, in which the party won 207 of the 294 seats, ending the 15-year rule of the Trinamool Congress, which was reduced to just 80 seats. Adhikari defeated Mamata Banerjee in Bhabanipur — considered one of the safest TMC strongholds — winning the seat by over 15,000 votes, delivering one of the biggest political shocks in recent Bengal history. Once a poster boy of the Trinamool Congress and a prominent figure in Banerjee's anti-land acquisition movement in Nandigram, Adhikari switched to the BJP in 2019 — a move that reshaped West Bengal's political dynamics and catapulted him to prominence.

**What to watch next:**
The government is expected to prove its majority on the floor of the Assembly within the next 10 days. Whether the BJP can translate its electoral triumph into stable and inclusive governance remains the central question as Suvendu Adhikari begins his innings as Chief Minister.

nri_angle: With West Bengal now under BJP rule for the first time, Indian-Americans with roots in the state — one of India's largest diaspora sources — will watch closely as Adhikari's new government shapes policy on law and order, education, and the Citizenship Amendment Act that directly affects Hindu refugee families many in the diaspora still have ties to.
author: Diaspora Desk
